 Where to feast on Thanksgiving Day 2026 at Dallas restaurants
 Stephanie Allmon Merry Oct 30, 2026 | 4:36 pm Thanksgiving spread at III Forks.
 Photo courtesy of III Forks
 The 2026 holiday season is upon us, and Thanksgiving is one of our favorite holidays because it revolves around food, and are thankful for that.
 The big day of feasting falls on Thursday, November 26, and Dallas-area restaurants are already getting in gear. From fine-dining dinners and traditional turkey plates to glorious brunch buffets and menus with a global twist, there are plenty of ways to let someone else do the cooking.
 The list below focuses on dine-in options, from family-friendly feasts to lavish spreads. All meals take place Thanksgiving Day only, unless noted. Reservation information and more details can be found on restaurant websites.
 Here’s where to enjoy a Thanksgiving meal at Dallas-area restaurants in 2026. And check back often. This list will grow as more restaurants unveil plans and menus.
 Alára : The modern Mediterranean restaurant in Oak Lawn will offer a five-course Thanksgiving-inspired prix fixe meal November 25 and 27 (but will not be open Thanksgiving Day). Menu features caramelized butternut squash ravioli, turkey roulade, and Turkish coffee-crusted hanger steak. Desserts include chocolate lava cake and wine-poached apple. Vegan and gluten-free options available; the regular à la carte menu will also be served. $125 per person.
 Asador : Renaissance Dallas Hotel restaurant will serve a Thanksgiving brunch buffet with an antipasto display, made-to-order omelets, New York strip carving station, herb-roasted turkey with giblet gravy, cranberry marmalade, brioche-apple stuffing, green bean and carrot casserole, and mac & cheese made with Vermont cheddar and smoked Gouda, plus assorted desserts. 10 am-3 pm, last seating at 2:30 pm. $90 per adult, $30 for children ages 6-12.
 ASTRA Kitchen + Lounge : The restaurant inside HALL Arts Hotel in the Dallas Arts District will serve a Thanksgiving prix fixe dinner featuring roasted pumpkin bisque, Southwest turkey roulade with cornbread stuffing and jalapeño cranberry sauce, and grilled filet mignon. Desserts include sweet potato crème brûlée and pecan pie with vanilla gelato. A Thanksgiving brunch will also be served from 6:30 am-3 pm. $85.
 Blue Mesa Grill : The Southwestern restaurant will serve a Thanksgiving buffet with roast turkey, smoked brisket, red chile-glazed ham, grilled salmon, cranberry-jalapeño relish, stuffing, mashed potatoes, butternut squash, green beans, and holiday pies. Additional stations offer made-to-order omelets, tacos, and Belgian waffles. 9 am-4 pm. $50 per adult, including mimosas and other beverages; $20 for children ages 6-11; free for children 5 and under. A Thanksgiving Family Pack to-go, featuring turkey and many trimmings, is also available for pre-order and pickup November 24-25; $175, details here .
 Centrale Italia : Preston Hollow Italian restaurant will serve a three-course Thanksgiving lunch with starters including butternut squash bisque with crab, pumpkin ricotta tortelloni, rock shrimp risotto, and roasted sweet potato with goat cheese and cranberry. Entrées include roasted turkey with Italian sausage-focaccia stuffing, grilled salmon, Barolo-glazed short rib, and Parmesan-crusted halibut. Desserts include pumpkin cheesecake, apple-blueberry crostata, tiramisu, and molten chocolate cake. 11 am-3 pm with a la carte specials repeated 4-9:30 pm. Lunch: $60 per person.
 Crown Block : The restaurant atop Reunion Tower will serve an all-you-can-eat Thanksgiving buffet with carving stations featuring prime rib, Cajun-fried and roasted turkey, and bone-in ham. Other offerings include green bean casserole, cornbread dressing, truffled deviled eggs, mac & cheese, sushi, fresh oysters, shrimp cocktail, smoked salmon, and gourmet cheeses. Desserts include bourbon pecan pie, caramel apple pie, pumpkin cheesecake, and dark chocolate silk pie. 11 am-6 pm. $165 per person. An early Thanksgiving brunch buffet will feature holiday favorites and à la carte options on November 22, 10:30 am-2:30 pm. $80.
 Docent Steak : The new Harwood steakhouse will offer an à la carte Thanksgiving menu with bacon-wrapped quail legs, a seafood tower, baby spinach salad, cuts of meat, and sides including a colossal baked potato, mac & cheese, and asparagus. 5-8:30 pm.
 HALL Park Hotel : The Frisco hotel will serve a Thanksgiving buffet with chef-attended carving stations featuring black truffle-rubbed prime rib, slow-roasted turkey with brown butter sage gravy, and apple cider pork belly. Other dishes include broiled salmon with blood orange cranberry gastrique, wild mushroom brioche dressing, and maple-glazed carrots with pecans. Desserts include pumpkin caramel cake, salted caramel apple pie cheesecake, pecan pie cookies, and gingerbread cupcakes. 11 am-4 pm. $95 per adult, $35 for children.
 The Henry Plano : The Legacy West restaurant will be open on Thanksgiving, serving its year-round dishes including cheesy truffle popovers, sprouts and squash salad, braised short rib, harvest bowl, mashed potatoes, mac & cheese, molten butter cake, and banana sticky toffee pudding. Prices vary.
 Jashan : The Michelin Guide-recommended Indian restaurant in Plano will offer a Thanksgiving prix fixe meal for families, alongside its regular menu. Available November 25-27. Prix fixe: $250 for a family of four.
 Kona Grill : The NorthPark Center restaurant will offer a Thanksgiving menu with traditional roasted turkey breast, whipped potatoes, green beans, stuffing, gravy, and cranberry sauce ($36), or macadamia nut-crusted turkey with shoyu cream and cranberry sauce ($39). A kids' turkey plate is $17, and pumpkin pie is $16. Available for dine-in and takeout Nov. 12-29; Thanksgiving takeout pickup 11 am-4 pm.
 Luna Roja : The Mexican restaurant inside Hilton Garden Inn Downtown Dallas will serve a three-course Thanksgiving dinner featuring Tijuana Caesar salad, ancho-orange roasted turkey with charred poblano mashed potatoes, seasonal vegetables, chile-mole turkey jus, and cinnamon tres leches. $45 per person.
 McRae’s American Bistro & Cocktails : The East Dallas restaurant will serve a two-course Thanksgiving dinner with a choice of tomato soup or Granny Smith salad, followed by roasted turkey breast, cornbread dressing, garlic mashed potatoes, green beans amandine, and cranberry sauce. À la carte options include filet mignon, salmon meunière, and lemon caper chicken. Bourbon pecan pie and vanilla crème brûlée are among the desserts. 11 am-6 pm. Prix fixe: $39 per adult, $15 for children under 12.
 Mercat Bistro : The French bistro will serve a three-course Thanksgiving brunch with smoked salmon, Quiche Lorraine, croissant eggs Benedict, turkey, steak frites, and desserts including pain perdu, chocolate tart, and beignets. Dinner options include escargot, roasted cauliflower soup, roasted turkey, petite filet, Parisian gnocchi, and pumpkin cheesecake. Brunch 10 am-3 pm, $75 per adult and $30 for children 12 and under; dinner 5-10 pm, $85 per adult and $35 for children 12 and under.
 Nobu Dallas : The Japanese restaurant will serve a Thanksgiving brunch buffet featuring sushi, pastries, desserts, chef-attended stations, and a turkey carving station. 11 am-2 pm. $95.
 The Ritz-Carlton Dallas, Las Colinas : The resort’s expansive Thanksgiving Mercato buffet will feature seafood, smoked salmon, artisan cheeses and charcuterie, herb-roasted turkey, hand-carved prime rib, cider-glazed ham, sweet potato casserole, and Cacio e Pepe prepared in a cheese wheel. Desserts include pumpkin profiteroles, spiced pumpkin crème brûlée, apple pie cheesecake, and maple pecan mille-feuille. 12-9 pm. $155 per adult, $55 for children ages 5-10.
 Saint Ann : The Harwood Street restaurant will serve a three-course Thanksgiving brunch with butternut squash soup, seared salmon, roasted turkey breast, and smoked brisket hash. Desserts include pumpkin pie, chocolate meringue pie, and apple pear crumble. 11 am-4 pm. $60 per person, $25 for children 12 and under.
 Silver Fox : The Richardson steakhouse will serve slow-roasted turkey with Grandma’s gravy, cornbread dressing, whipped potatoes, candied yams, sugar snap peas, and spiced cranberry sauce. Kentucky bourbon pecan pie and pumpkin pie are among the desserts. 12-6 pm. $45 per adult, $20 for children 12 and under. A family meal pack with the same menu is also available for takeout, with prices varying by group size. Preorders begin November 17.
 Stillwell’s Steakhouse : The Hotel Swexan steakhouse will offer its regular à la carte menu alongside a Thanksgiving turkey roulade with stuffing, butterscotch heirloom carrots, spiced Texas pecans, gravy, and cranberry mostarda. Bookings begin at 5 pm.
 III Forks : Both Addison and Frisco locations of the steakhouse will serve a three-course Thanksgiving dinner with spice-rubbed turkey, Grandma’s gravy, cranberry-orange relish, sausage-sage cornbread dressing, creamed potatoes, maple-glazed yams, and roasted autumn vegetables. Desserts include Kentucky bourbon chocolate pecan pie and pumpkin pie cake. 11 am-8 pm. $45 per adult, $20 for children 12 and under. A turkey family meal pack is also available for takeout, with prices varying by group size. Preorders begin November 17.
 Winsome Prime : Dallas restaurant will serve its full brunch menu along with a Thanksgiving dinner option of smoked turkey or Hawaiian-glazed ham with two sides, including cornbread dressing, garlic truffle mashed potatoes, mac & cheese, or greens, and cranberry sauce. Desserts include Mama’s carrot cake and sweet potato pie. 10 am-4 pm. $35 per person.

 Fosters Crossing Pecans debuts 2026 crop at its farm in Anna
 Teresa Gubbins Oct 30, 2026 | 3:15 pm 
 Photo courtesy of Fosters Crossing Pecans
 Fosters Crossing Pecans
 The 2026 pecan season has arrived in Texas and you can buy them fresh at Foster Crossing Pecans , a pecan grower in Anna at 1303 W. Foster Crossing Rd.
 These are different from pecans sold in supermarkets year-round, says Foster Crossing Pecans founder Jim Luscombe. 
 "Pecans sold at grocery stores are good, but they've been stored for a while," Luscombe says. "You're not going to believe how good fresh pecans are."
 Foster Crossing is one of the many family pecan farmers across Texas, often passed down through multiple generations, although the number of farmers is decreasing. But more of those remaining growers are pivoting in the same direction as Foster Crossing and selling directly to consumers.
 For Luscombe, Foster Crossing Pecans was a second act. He and his wife Robyn founded the company in 2002, planting a first stand of 100 pecan trees on farmland his family had owned since around 1875.
 "I had a great career in the computer industry, and when I got ready to retire, I decided to come back to one of the family farms," he says. "It had two nice native pecan orchards. There was pecan history with my grandparents, too. So I started with 100 trees, then another 100. I really enjoy the process of growing them and seeing them mature."
 He now has more than 500 improved variety trees along with numerous grand native pecan trees, some estimated to be hundreds of years old.
 Foster Crossing Pecans owners Robyn and Jim Luscombe do their rendition of the "American Gothic" pose.. Photo courtesy of Foster Crossing Pecans 
 He plants a variety called paper shell, prized for both their delicate shell and their rich, buttery flavor.
 "Paper shell are the most sought after because the shells are thin enough to crack easily, and the 'mammoth' size we grow are large enough to make them worth picking up and cracking," Luscombe says. "Over the years, plant experts have improved varieties, resulting in pecans that look good and taste good."
 It's a long-term commitment, since pecan trees don't start producing pecans right away.
 "A native pecan tree takes about 13 or 14 years before you see pecans," Luscombe says. "If you go to A&M, they've bred more productive pecan trees that bear fruit as quickly as eight or nine years."
 This year's crop 
The Texas harvest for 2026 is estimated to be 39 million pounds of pecans, an increase from the past few years. Pecan season runs from late September through January, depending on region. In North Texas, the harvest begins in late October and runs through December.
 Foster Crossing will open its 2026 season on October 30, selling fresh crop pecans and offering custom cracking at their barn at 1303 W. Foster Crossing Rd. on Thursdays-Saturdays from 9 am-4 pm every weekend until the season ends.
 They offer a variety of formats:
 Pecans in the shell, one pound for $8.25
 Cracked-Only Pecans, with the shell partially cracked. You finish shelling and picking, 3 pounds for $25
 Custom Shelled - Shelled pecan halves, to display on top of pies and pecan candies, one pound for $18
 Choppers - Larger pieces, but not whole halves, 3 pounds for $48
 They'll sell upwards of 5,000 pounds of pecans, and they sell out every year.
 They'll also take your backyard crop and shell them for you, $1 per pound for small native pecans to crack, shell, and run them through the blower to get rid of shell residue.
 Pecan Therapy 
Lubscombe is a highly engaging fellow and great listener who jokes that they provide "Pecan Therapy at no charge," encouraging all to visit, help crack pecans, sit on the porch, and watch the sunset.
 "I have memories from when I was young of being with my dad and my granddad and mamaw — everybody had one of those round wooden bowls with the pecan cracker and the little pickers, sitting and cracking and picking the meat out," he says. "Doing that gave you a chance to talk and visit a little bit."
 It's an intrinsic part of the company ethos.
 "Foster Crossing brings great enjoyment for me," he says. "I am not making any money, but I get to meet wonderful people. Everyone is happy to be here and get pecans. Many are repeat customers, year after year. They started with us as couples. In some cases, one of the spouses has passed. Or the people who once picked and shelled pecans with their grandparents. Part of our service is to stop and listen to folks who want to tell you their stories. We've discovered that it's important to listen to them as part of our pecan therapy."
